articles.headline: Lugo Monumental Takes Low-Emission Zone Ordinance to Court
articles.subtitle: The association representing city-centre traders and hospitality businesses will challenge the newly approved ZBE ordinance, arguing it is poorly drafted, restricts disabled parking to two hours and lacks a pollution basis
articles.body: Lugo Monumental, the association that groups shopkeepers and hospitality businesses in Lugo's city centre, has voted to take the newly approved Zona de Bajas Emisiones ordinance to court after the Concello rejected its objections. The low-emission zone, approved in the last plenary session, is due to come into force at the end of summer, though fines will not be imposed during the first year. The association argues the ordinance is easily annullable because it is poorly drafted and contains errors that were not corrected before approval. Among the specific points of contention is a rule limiting disabled parking spaces to two hours, which the association says effectively prevents people with reduced mobility from having a meal in the city centre. Lugo Monumental also questions the fundamental basis of the ordinance, arguing that traffic restrictions in the centre lack justification when there are no pollution problems, given that the area is already largely pedestrianised. The group points to the approach taken in Ponferrada, where restrictions are tied to real-time air quality measurements, as a more reasonable model. A total of 41 objections were filed against the ordinance by ten different parties, including the PP and Lugo Monumental.

articles.headline: Roman Gold Mine Discovered in Pastoriza During Quarry Expansion
articles.subtitle: Survey work for a quarry extension in Campo do Oso, on the border with Mondoñedo, has revealed the extent of a large-scale Roman gold extraction operation that was active some 2,000 years ago
articles.body: A significant Roman gold mining site has been identified in the northern part of the municipality of Pastoriza, in the Campo do Oso area near the boundary with Mondoñedo. The discovery came about through routine survey work required for the expansion of a local quarry, which allowed archaeologists to delimit the radius of an extraction operation that was active roughly two millennia ago. The site adds to a growing picture of Roman mining activity in the province of Lugo, which was one of the most important gold-producing regions in the Roman Empire. The Romans employed hydraulic mining techniques, using water channels to break down hillsides and extract gold from the alluvial deposits. Lugo province already contains several known Roman gold workings, including the spectacular Mina da Toca, but the Pastoriza find extends the known distribution of these operations further north. The discovery was reported by La Voz de Galicia, which noted that the site lies a short distance from the A-8 motorway. Further study will be needed to determine the full scale of the operation and whether any associated settlement remains are present.

articles.headline: Xunta Funds Conservation Plan for Piornedo's Ancient Pallozas
articles.subtitle: A 100,000-euro agreement with the Ser Association will produce the technical documentation for a comprehensive plan to save the last surviving thatched stone roundhouses in Galicia, declared a Bien de Interés Cultural
articles.body: The Xunta de Galicia is to allocate 100,000 euros for the preparation of technical documentation needed to draw up a comprehensive conservation and rehabilitation plan for the pallozas of Piornedo, the only surviving examples of these traditional thatched stone roundhouses in all of Galicia. The agreement, to be presented to the Consello da Xunta on Monday, establishes a collaboration with the Ser Association, a non-profit cultural organisation based in Os Ancares. The funding will be spread over two years, with 70,000 euros in 2026 and 30,000 in 2027. The Ser Association will carry out research and studies to establish the procedures and construction techniques needed for the conservation and restoration of the pallozas, which are declared a Bien de Interés Cultural. The association will also seek European funds for complementary financing of further interventions. The plan will include repair work on selected pallozas based on their state of conservation and heritage interest. The pallozas of Piornedo have been deteriorating for years due to a lack of maintenance funding, with some owners resorting to corrugated metal roofing as a stopgap. The new plan aims to establish a sustainable long-term maintenance programme.

articles.headline: Tragic End to Search for Missing 24-Year-Old in Lugo
articles.subtitle: The body of Carmen López Rebolo, who disappeared on 21 July, was found on Friday morning in the A Cheda area. Police have ruled out criminal violence and the main hypothesis is suicide
articles.body: The body of Carmen López Rebolo, the 24-year-old woman who had been missing in Lugo since 21 July, was found on Friday morning in the A Cheda area. The discovery brought a tragic end to a ten-day search that had mobilised police, volunteers and the local community. Police sources confirmed that the body was found in a wooded area and that the initial investigation has ruled out the involvement of third parties. The main hypothesis being investigated is that she took her own life. The young woman was last seen in the A Milagrosa neighbourhood of Lugo on 21 July, and her disappearance had prompted widespread concern and an extensive search operation involving ground, water and air resources. The National Police released details of how the body was located, confirming that there was no evidence of robbery or violent death. The case has deeply affected the local community, with messages of condolence appearing on social media and from local organisations. The family has requested privacy during this time.

articles.headline: Ceuta Death Toll Reaches 67 as Spain Installs Floating Sea Barrier
articles.subtitle: A 500-metre pneumatic barrier is being laid at the Tarajal breakwater after some 60,000 people crossed from Morocco. Spain says 48,300 have returned, but the King has expressed indignation and Sánchez has called for an urgent EU meeting
articles.body: The death toll from the mass border crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta has risen to at least 67, the Spanish government confirmed on Saturday, as authorities began installing a 500-metre floating barrier at the Tarajal breakwater. The pneumatic barrier, designed to stand 30 to 70 centimetres above the water and extend up to a metre below the surface, runs parallel to a line of anchored buoys with a channel for Civil Guard patrol vessels. The measure responds to a ruling by Spain's Supreme Court that migrants intercepted at sea cannot be summarily returned unless they have bypassed a physical barrier. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who visited Ceuta on Friday, blamed human trafficking networks for exploiting the ruling. Spain's Interior Ministry said more than 48,300 of the estimated 50,000 to 60,000 people who entered the territory since Thursday had returned to Morocco by late Friday. King Felipe VI issued a statement expressing his great concern and indignation at the grave events, calling on the state to adopt all necessary measures to ensure the security of Ceuta and Melilla and to prevent such incidents from recurring. The King has been in contact with Sánchez, opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, and the presidents of both autonomous cities.

articles.headline: Sánchez Demands Urgent EU Meeting After Italy Suspends Schengen With Spain
articles.subtitle: The Spanish prime minister accused some EU member states of a selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction to the Ceuta crisis, as Italy closed air and sea borders for one month and 22 EU nations called for emergency talks
articles.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called for an urgent video conference of EU interior ministers after Italy announced a one-month suspension of the Schengen free-travel agreement with Spain, closing its air and sea borders. In a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa and Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, whose country holds the EU presidency, Sánchez said he had been deeply concerned by the reaction of some EU governments. While most had expressed support, others had chosen to attack Spain and call for its temporary exclusion from the Schengen area. Such an attitude, he wrote, was contrary to European law, humanitarian law and the principles of solidarity that bind the union together. In a pointed rebuke to Italy, he noted that Spain was one of the least porous external borders of the EU, with irregular entries half those recorded in Italy between 2021 and 2026. Von der Leyen said the EU had offered Spain support from the first moment and that lessons must be learned. EU interior ministers will meet by videoconference on Tuesday. France's Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said Spain did not need to leave Schengen, while 22 EU member states signed an open letter demanding an urgent meeting. The crisis has inflamed the political divide on migration within the EU.

articles.headline: King Felipe VI Expresses Indignation Over Ceuta Crisis
articles.subtitle: The monarch said the state must guarantee the security of Ceuta and Melilla and prevent a repeat of the grave events that have resulted in the tragic loss of dozens of lives, after days of contact with political leaders
articles.body: King Felipe VI has expressed his great concern and indignation at the grave events in Ceuta, and to a lesser extent Melilla, in a statement released by the Royal Household on Saturday. The head of state said he had been in contact over recent days with Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, and the presidents of both autonomous cities. The King stressed the need to adopt all necessary measures to convey in a united, clear and determined manner the support and affection of the rest of Spain to the populations of Ceuta and Melilla. The state must guarantee their security and prevent these events, which have resulted in the tragic loss of dozens of lives, from recurring, he said. The statement came as the government reported that the situation in Ceuta had been largely reversed, with the border restored to calm and the majority of those who entered having returned to Morocco. However, the president of Ceuta, Juan Jesús Vivas, said the city had not returned to normal, with many migrants still on the streets and residents expressing concern. The King's intervention underscores the gravity with which the crisis is viewed at the highest level of the Spanish state.

articles.headline: US and Israel Prepare Major Strikes on Iran's Energy Infrastructure
articles.subtitle: Washington is weighing weekend military action against Iranian power plants and refineries, sources told CBS News, as Trump withholds final approval. Iran has threatened to hit regional energy sites in retaliation
articles.body: The United States and Israel are preparing to bombard energy-related targets in Iran as soon as this weekend, according to sources familiar with the matter who spoke to CBS News, though no final decision has been made. The planned strikes would target Iranian power plants, refineries and other energy infrastructure, representing a significant escalation in the conflict that began in February. The Pentagon has previously struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets inside Iran in retaliation for attacks on American bases in Jordan. Iran has warned that it would respond by hitting energy infrastructure across the region if its own power plants are targeted, a threat that has kept global energy markets on edge. The Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil passes, has been a recurring flashpoint. The conflict has already drawn in multiple countries, with a drone striking a US-owned LNG tanker at the Egyptian port of Damietta last week, the first attack on Egyptian soil. Saudi Arabia has proposed a maritime defence alliance that fourteen countries have backed. The potential strikes on energy infrastructure mark a new phase in a conflict that has already expanded far beyond its original participants.

articles.headline: Ceuta Crisis Reverberates Across Europe as 22 EU States Demand Talks
articles.subtitle: The mass border crossing into Spain's North African enclave has triggered a political crisis in the EU, with Italy suspending Schengen, France reinforcing border controls, and Germany's Merz calling for Morocco to take back migrants without delay
articles.body: The mass border crossing into Ceuta has sent shockwaves through the European Union, exposing deep divisions over migration policy. Italy announced a one-month suspension of the Schengen free-travel agreement with Spain, closing its air and sea borders. Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani called the measure unavoidable, blaming Spain's decision to regularise more than one million undocumented migrants for incentivising human trafficking. France reinforced border controls with Spain while stopping short of calling for Spain's suspension from Schengen. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said Spain did not need to leave the zone and that cooperation remained strong. Germany's Friedrich Merz called on Morocco to take back the irregular migrants without delay. Denmark and Finland also called for reconsidering Spain's participation in the Schengen agreement. In response, 22 of the 27 EU member states signed an open letter demanding an urgent video meeting of interior ministers. Spain's Sánchez accused some member states of a selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction, noting that Spain had one of the least porous external borders in the EU. The European Commission said it had offered Spain support from the first moment. The crisis has inflamed the already bitter political divide on migration within the EU, with far-right leaders across the continent seizing on the events to push for stricter border controls.

articles.headline: FTC Approves IonQ's $1.8 Billion Acquisition of SkyWater Semiconductor Foundry
articles.subtitle: The Federal Trade Commission split 1-1 on whether to impose conditions, allowing the deal to close. The merger creates the only vertically integrated full-stack quantum computing platform company with a US-based foundry
articles.body: IonQ has received final regulatory approval to complete its $1.8 billion acquisition of SkyWater Technology, the largest exclusively US-based semiconductor foundry, after the Federal Trade Commission was unable to decide whether to impose conditions on the deal. The FTC split 1-1 on accepting a settlement that would have required IonQ to pledge not to disadvantage rivals that contract with SkyWater. FTC Commissioner Andrew Ferguson said that because the two could not agree on an order setting conditions, the next-best option was to get out of the way and permit the merger to close. The combined company will be the only vertically integrated full-stack quantum platform company, combining IonQ's quantum computing technology with SkyWater's semiconductor manufacturing capabilities. SkyWater will continue to serve its existing customers as a US-based foundry. The companies expect to hold their second quarter earnings call on 5 August and an investor day in the third quarter. The deal closed on 31 July, marking a significant milestone in the quantum computing industry, where access to specialised chip manufacturing is increasingly seen as a strategic advantage. The acquisition had been under regulatory review since earlier this year.

articles.headline: German Court Rules AI Music Generator Suno Violated Copyright
articles.subtitle: The Munich Regional Court found that Suno trained on GEMA-represented songs without permission and reproduced recognisable melodies, in one of Europe's first binding decisions on AI-generated music. Suno must disclose revenue for damages calculation
articles.body: A German court has ruled that Suno, one of the world's most popular AI music generators, violated copyright law by training on protected songs without permission, in what legal experts describe as one of Europe's first binding decisions on AI-generated music. The Munich Regional Court found on 31 July that Suno had no right to process the work of artists represented by GEMA, Germany's state-mandated licensing body, after evidence showed its system had memorised and reproduced their songs. In court, GEMA played side-by-side comparisons of Suno's output and famous tracks including Forever Young, Mambo No. 5 and Daddy Cool, arguing the AI reproduced recognisable melodies, harmonies and rhythms. The court agreed that Suno had memorised and reproduced six GEMA-represented songs during training. Suno must now hand over information on the revenue it earned from the infringement so that damages can be calculated. Under German law, a first-instance judgment can be enforced even while an appeal is pending, meaning GEMA could pursue injunctions against Suno's European operations immediately. The Massachusetts-based startup, valued at around $5.4 billion, said it is evaluating its options including an appeal. The ruling is the latest in a series of legal challenges facing AI music companies, with Sony also suing rival Udio over 30,000 songs.

articles.headline: EU AI Act Transparency Rules Take Effect on 2 August
articles.subtitle: The European Union's landmark AI regulation reaches a key milestone as transparency obligations under Article 50 become enforceable, requiring providers and deployers of AI systems to label AI-generated content and disclose training data
articles.body: The European Union's AI Act reaches a significant enforcement milestone on 2 August 2026, as transparency obligations under Article 50 become applicable. The rules require providers and deployers of AI systems to clearly label AI-generated content, including deepfakes and text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest. The obligations apply to both providers who develop AI systems and deployers who use them, making this the most widely applicable section of the Act. The transparency rules cover chatbots, generative AI systems and other AI tools that interact with users or produce content. Providers must ensure that AI-generated content is identifiable through machine-readable markings, though a transitional period until 2 December 2026 applies for systems already on the market before August 2. The enforcement of these rules coincides with the activation of the AI Office's supervisory and fining authority over general-purpose AI model providers, who have technically been obligated since August 2025 but now face actual enforcement. The general penalty ceiling under Article 99 is 15 million euros or 3 percent of global annual turnover. The high-risk AI system obligations have been deferred to December 2027 under the Digital Omnibus, but the transparency rules remain on schedule. The European Commission published guidelines on the transparency obligations in July 2026.

articles.headline: EU AI Act Transparency Rules Come Into Force Across Europe
articles.subtitle: From 2 August, providers and deployers of AI systems in the EU must label AI-generated content and disclose when users are interacting with a chatbot, marking the first major enforceable deadline of the landmark regulation
articles.body: The European Union's AI Act reaches its first major enforceable milestone on 2 August 2026, as the transparency obligations under Article 50 come into full effect. The rules apply to any organisation that provides or deploys AI systems within the EU, regardless of where the company is based. Under the new rules, providers of generative AI systems must ensure that AI-generated content is identifiable through machine-readable markings. Deployers must clearly label deepfakes and any AI-generated text published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest. Chatbots and other AI systems that interact with users must disclose that the user is interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the context. The European Commission published detailed guidelines on the transparency obligations in July 2026, providing practical guidance on compliance. The AI Office now has supervisory and fining authority over general-purpose AI model providers, with penalties of up to 15 million euros or 3 percent of global annual turnover. The rules represent the first binding transparency requirements for AI systems at this scale anywhere in the world. While the high-risk AI obligations have been deferred to December 2027 under the Digital Omnibus, the transparency rules proceed on schedule. The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024, with a phased implementation timeline that reaches this key milestone today.

articles.headline: German Court Sets Landmark Precedent on AI Music Copyright
articles.subtitle: The Munich ruling against Suno is one of Europe's first binding decisions on whether AI training on copyrighted music requires permission, with implications for the entire generative AI industry across the continent
articles.body: The Munich Regional Court's ruling against AI music generator Suno marks a significant legal precedent for the AI industry in Europe, establishing that training AI models on copyrighted music without permission constitutes infringement. The court found that Suno had memorised and reproduced six songs represented by GEMA, Germany's state-mandated licensing body, including recognisable hits such as Forever Young, Mambo No. 5 and Daddy Cool. The ruling is particularly significant because it addresses the core question at the heart of many pending AI copyright cases: whether the use of copyrighted material for AI training requires a licence. The court's answer is unequivocally yes, at least under German law. The decision is appealable, but under German law, a first-instance judgment can be enforced immediately, meaning GEMA could pursue injunctions against Suno's European operations without waiting for the appeals process. The ruling follows the same court's 2025 decision that OpenAI's ChatGPT had infringed copyright by reproducing German song lyrics, establishing Munich as an unlikely centre of gravity for AI copyright law. The decision has implications beyond music, as the same legal principles could apply to text, images and video training data. AI companies across Europe are now reviewing their training data practices in light of the ruling, which provides the clearest judicial guidance yet on the legality of training on copyrighted works without permission.
